problem: Existing VLN systems struggle with edge-side inference, platform compatibility and task extensibility; most rely on cloud-based large models and are hard to deploy on resource-constrained devices.
motivation: Embodied VLN must run efficiently on-device on heterogeneous robots with plug-and-play generalization. The paper draws on the modular architecture of human cognition to reduce computational redundancy while keeping accuracy.
key_idea: Decouple the VLN pipeline into hierarchical modules with edge-optimized multimodal fusion so the whole system runs on-device with semantic alignment and cloud-level accuracy.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so ablations are not visible. The abstract suggests that modular decoupling and removing computational redundancy in retrieval and fusion account for the edge-side efficiency gains without losing accuracy.
method: Hierarchical modular framework: decouples the navigation pipeline into computational modules, all deployable on-device
Edge-optimized multimodal fusion: aligns vision and language semantically while removing redundant computation
Efficient retrieval module: claimed 11.5x retrieval efficiency improvement
Plug-and-play design: supports zero-shot dynamic and region navigation tasks and heterogeneous robot platforms
numbers_note: abstract only; no per-benchmark metrics given (only relative claims: 11.5x retrieval efficiency, 1.46x navigation accuracy on the edge vs. existing edge methods, 5.93x lower latency vs. best cloud method)
results: VLONS reports an 11.5x retrieval efficiency gain and 1.46x navigation accuracy over existing edge-side methods, while matching cloud-based accuracy. It has 5.93x lower inference latency than the previous best cloud method, and it was deployed on multiple robotic platforms.
limitations: Abstract gives no benchmarks or absolute metrics, so the claims cannot be verified
